Since \(p_2\mid p_1\), let \(q=\frac{p_1}{p_2}\in\mathbb Z\). Then
\[
p_1p_2=10! \implies qp_2^2=10!,
\]
so \(p_2^2\mid 10!\).

Now
\[
10! = 2^8\cdot 3^4\cdot 5^2\cdot 7 = 720^2\cdot 7.
\]
Thus \(p_2^2\mid 720^2\cdot 7\), so \(p_2\mid 720\). Hence \(p_2\le 720\), and
\[
\frac{p_1}{p_2}=\frac{10!}{p_2^2}\ge \frac{10!}{720^2}=7.
\]

This is achievable: take the second group as \(\{8,9,10\}\), so
\[
p_2=8\cdot 9\cdot 10=720,
\]
and the first group is \(\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7\}\), with
\[
p_1=1\cdot2\cdot3\cdot4\cdot5\cdot6\cdot7=5040.
\]
Then \(\frac{p_1}{p_2}=\frac{5040}{720}=7\).

\[
\boxed{7}
\]
